solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: US president against opposing wings in equal measure

parts.note: George Bush, father or son, was a US president

indicators.note: the two opposite wings of the word equal are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A political commentator says a US president stands against both extremes in equal measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposing wings in' picks the outside letters of 'equal', E and L; 'against' just sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushel is an old unit of dry capacity, a standard measure for grain.

clue.text: Extra group of students in university education

indicators.note: the students' group is placed within the university and education letters

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students, a British students' body

explanation.surface: An extra group of students has joined a university education course.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unused is spare, left over beyond what was needed, so it is surplus or extra.

clue.text: Animal trainer clamps front of bridle with a part for rider to grip

indicators.note: the trainer word grips the other letters inside it, as a clamp holds something

parts.note: a handler trains and controls animals such as dogs

indicators.note: the front of bridle is its first letter

explanation.surface: An animal trainer holds the front of a bridle together with a part a rider grips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clamps' puts B (front of 'bridle') and A inside HANDLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Handlebars are the bar a cyclist holds to steer, the part a rider grips.

clue.text: Witnesses lad following attractive person

indicators.note: the lad's word comes after the attractive person's word

parts.note: a looker is informal for a good-looking person
a son is a lad, a boy

explanation.surface: Witnesses see a young lad trailing after a beautiful person.
explanation.definitionFit: Onlookers are people who watch an event without taking part, i.e. spectators or witnesses.

clue.text: Vehicle going round a lake and river valley in Italian region

indicators.note: the vehicle word goes around the next letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a cab is a taxi, a vehicle
L is the map abbreviation for lake
a ria is a long narrow inlet formed by a drowned river valley

explanation.surface: A car tours a lake and a river valley in a region of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts A and L inside CAB, giving CALAB. A ria is a river valley the sea has flooded.
explanation.definitionFit: Calabria is the region at the toe of the Italian peninsula.

clue.text: Mournful song's line chanted differently with twist

indicators.note: the twisting word is added after the rearranged letters
the letters of line chanted are set out in a different order

parts.note: to wind is to twist or coil

explanation.surface: A sad song has a line sung in a new way, with a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' is the anagram signal; 'Mournful song's' reads as 'the mournful song is', the 's a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Elton John's ballad, rewritten as a lament for Princess Diana in 1997, is a famously mournful song.

clue.text: Knight supporting king as master

indicators.note: in a down answer, the knight's letter sits below and props up the king

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's legendary king
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight serves as the support of a king acting as his lord and master.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' means placed underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a skill is to learn it thoroughly, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Bump boat

definitions.meaning: to collide clumsily with someone, as in pushing through a crowd
a flat-bottomed vessel used on canals and rivers

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both the verb meaning jostle or knock and the noun naming a canal vessel.

clue.text: Loose cover draped around middle of deck

indicators.note: the cover word is wrapped around the other letters

parts.note: to insure something is to give it financial cover

indicators.note: the middle of deck is its two central letters

explanation.surface: A loose cover is draped across the middle of a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draped around' tells you the cover word wraps round the centre letters of 'deck'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insecure is not firmly fixed, so it is loose or wobbly.

clue.text: Tango drink covering container for refuse

indicators.note: the drink word sits against the container word, joined to it in the charade

parts.note: T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an urn is a vessel or container
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: A tango dancer drinks while a bin for rubbish stands nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' is a verb here, not rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an offer is to decline or reject it.

clue.text: He's far at sea, once more

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sailor is far out at sea once again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges HESFAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something afresh means starting it again, a new time.

clue.text: Turned poorly, squeezed into small footwear

indicators.note: the turned letters are pushed inside the small word

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: turned means the poorly word is read backwards

parts.note: poorly means ill

explanation.surface: Someone fell ill after squeezing into shoes too small for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' signals the reversal and 'squeezed into' the insertion. A wellie is a British rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellie is a wellington, a waterproof rubber boot, so a piece of footwear.

clue.text: Criminal nicely drawing in opponents showing mercy

indicators.note: the rearranged letters pull the opponents' letters inside
criminal means bad or wrong, so the letters are put in a wrong order

parts.note: E and N are opponents at bridge, East and North sitting opposite

explanation.surface: A criminal who charmingly wins over his rivals is shown mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges the fodder into LENICY; 'opponents' are East and North, rivals across the bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: Leniency is a gentle, forgiving attitude to punishment, close in sense to clemency.

clue.text: Leader in boat requesting quiet with ship following marine creature

indicators.note: the ship's word comes after the quiet one
the leader in boat is its first letter

parts.note: requesting means asking
sh is a call for quiet
the ark is Noah's ship

explanation.surface: The skipper of a boat asks for silence as a ship trails a sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The basking shark is a huge plankton-eating fish, a sea creature named for lounging at the surface.

clue.text: Test subject — old tender pigeon with age ignored

parts.note: the guinea was an old British gold coin, legal tender

indicators.note: the age's letters are left out of pigeon

parts.note: an eon is an age

explanation.surface: An ageing pigeon is offered as an old subject for testing.
explanation.walkthrough: A guinea was an old British coin worth 21 shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for anyone used in an experiment comes from rodents used in labs.

clue.text: Director's prickling sensation constant in joint

indicators.note: the sensation and constant letters go within the joint word

parts.note: the hock is the joint in an animal's hind leg
an itch is a prickling feeling on the skin
C is the symbol for the speed of light, a physical constant

explanation.surface: A film director feels a constant tingle in one of his joints.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Hitchcock was the British film director of Psycho and Vertigo.

clue.text: Most speedy escape from ordeal

parts.note: to flee is to escape
a test is a trial or ordeal

explanation.surface: The quickest person gets away from a painful trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet means swift, so its superlative means the very fastest.

clue.text: Player at home in Bordeaux strip's regularly first to tackle

indicators.note: the at-home word goes within the Bordeaux word

parts.note: claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine
in means at home

indicators.note: every other letter of strip's is taken
the first letter of tackle

explanation.surface: A footballer relaxes at home with Bordeaux while his team's kit shows his tackling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes alternate letters of STRIPS, giving TIS; 'first to tackle' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinettist is a musician who plays the clarinet, a woodwind player.

clue.text: Finish shift after introducing new head of engineering

indicators.note: the shift word takes the new letters into its middle

parts.note: to veer is to change direction, shift

indicators.note: the head of engineering is its first letter

explanation.surface: A worker finishes a shift after the new chief engineer is introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: N and E (head of 'engineering') go inside VEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin decorative surface layer on furniture, a finish.

clue.text: After refurbishment, see if lab is workable

indicators.note: refurbishing remakes something, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Once the laboratory has been refitted, check whether it is usable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After refurbishment' rearranges SEEIFLAB; 'is' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A feasible plan is one that can be carried out, practicable.

clue.text: Great meal apart from starter of prawns

indicators.note: the meal word is taken without the starter letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

indicators.note: the starter of prawns is its first letter

explanation.surface: A great dinner, apart from the prawn cocktail starter.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPPER loses one P, the first letter of 'prawns'.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal praise meaning excellent or terrific.

clue.text: Erected hard bed made of wood

indicators.note: in a down answer, putting up the letters means reading them from bottom to top

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
a crib is a baby's bed

explanation.surface: A sturdy bed has been put up, built from wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erected' reverses HCRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Birch is the timber of a slender tree with white bark.

clue.text: Sounds reverberating from city hotel lovers occasionally used

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: only some letters, every other one, of lovers are taken

explanation.surface: Noises carry through a city hotel that couples sometimes use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes alternate letters of 'lovers', giving OES. EC is the City of London postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoes are sounds bouncing back off surfaces, i.e. repeated reflections of noise.

clue.text: Revolutionary agent encountered moderate

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a rep is a representative or sales agent
met means encountered

explanation.surface: A revolutionary secret agent met someone with a calming influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reverses REPMET.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to tone it down, soften or moderate it.

clue.text: Unseemly Cockney's that man with crutch coming before the Queen

indicators.note: the crutch word precedes the Queen's letters

parts.note: a Cockney drops the h, saying him as 'im
a crutch is a prop or support
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A Londoner thinks it rude of a man on a crutch to push in ahead of the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop their h's.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper conduct is unbecoming or indecent, not fitting the occasion.

clue.text: Made rigid cart, developed in outhouse

indicators.note: the developed letters go within the outhouse word

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A cart, put together in a shed, was made sturdy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges CART to TARC.
explanation.definitionFit: Starched fabric has been stiffened with starch, so made stiff.

clue.text: Fine picture on rear of big racing vehicle

indicators.note: the rear of big is its last letter

parts.note: OK means fine
art is pictures, paintings

explanation.surface: A fine painting is propped against the back of a large racing car.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-kart is a small open motor vehicle raced on tracks.
